draft.personalized_opening: Your profile links Outlaw Territories to environments of insecurity and architectural governance (https://www.arch.columbia.edu/faculty/29-felicity-scott). That raises a precise question for the study: where does authorization acquire a physical boundary?

draft.body:
Dear Professor Felicity Scott,

Your profile links Outlaw Territories to environments of insecurity and architectural governance (https://www.arch.columbia.edu/faculty/29-felicity-scott). That raises a precise question for the study: where does authorization acquire a physical boundary?

I’m developing Proxy Society, an architecture research project on AI agents and robots acting for absent people under limited, revocable mandates. I would compare a staffed library entrance with a gated proxy handoff recess: the same limited instruction and expiry, but different paths to question a refusal, revoke the instruction and enter personally. The plans would test how an apparently convenient service becomes spatial governance.

Could you advise whether this belongs in an architecture history/theory dissertation, and which historical counterexample would challenge the premise before developing prototypes?

Best regards,
Kris Haamer

Dear Professor Reinhold Martin,

The Organizational Complex connects corporate space, media and cybernetics in your published profile (https://www.arch.columbia.edu/faculty/17-reinhold-martin). I want to use that institutional scale to question a small reception transaction.

Dear Professor Hiba Bou Akar,

For the War Yet to Come examines how planning produces contested frontiers through anticipated conflict (https://www.arch.columbia.edu/faculty/518-hiba-bou-akar). I want to test how a much smaller civic threshold anticipates and organizes risk.

Your profile’s Design and Political Dissent and research on spatial agency and maintenance connect participation to material arrangements (https://www.newschool.edu/parsons/faculty/Georgia-Traganou/). They offer a way to question what a proxy actually displaces.
